# Routing & Assignment

`customer_support.intake_and_triage.routing_and_assignment` · v0.1.0 · **draft** · **STUB**

**Which queue can finish this, and which person should hold it?**


> Choosing the queue and then choosing the human, which are two decisions with different failure modes and are usually run as one. Queue routing fails on taxonomy — a ticket with no obvious home lands in the largest queue and ages there, unowned and apparently handled. Assignment fails on load and on skill, and load is the one organisations optimise because it is the one a dashboard can see. The judgement that separates a good router from a fair one is knowing when to break the rule for continuity: an account that has been working with a specific agent through a long-running problem loses more to a fresh, well-balanced owner than the queue gains from the balance. Assignment without a named human is not assignment, it is deferral with extra steps.

> Stub — identity, purpose and load-set only. Promote by separating the two decisions explicitly through every section: queue-level playbooks and heuristics, then person-level ones, and failure_modes for each. The highest-value content is the continuity-versus-capacity trade and the rules for when round-robin should be suspended (named accounts, active escalations, reopened tickets, anything an agent has already apologised for). KPIs must include unowned-queue ageing alongside per-agent load, because a perfectly balanced roster sitting next to an ageing catch-all queue reads as healthy. Handoffs: upstream from ticket_triage, parallel with queue_management and workload_balancing, downstream into diagnostics and escalation_management.
